content.title: About
content.content: Yellow rice is processed rice that is cooked with added fat (usually vegetable oil or clarified butter) and spices such as turmeric or saffron, which give it a characteristic golden colour and aroma. The product is ready to eat and is commonly used as a side dish for meat, fish, and vegetable meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yellow rice is traditionally prepared in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and South Asian cuisines.
Adding fat increases the calorie density, making the dish more satiating.
Turmeric, often used for coloring, has anti‑inflammatory properties.
Saffron, though expensive, imparts a vivid golden hue and a unique fragrance.
In many cultures yellow rice is served on festive occasions as a symbol of abundance.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrates provide quick glucose for the body’s energy needs.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: The added vegetable fat supplies monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties of turmeric
items.content: Turmeric’s curcumin acts as an antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory agent.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Easily digestible rice can be gentle on the stomach and suitable for low‑fiber diets.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Added fat raises the calorie count, so portion control is important for weight management.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to turmeric, saffron, or other added seasonings.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared versions may contain salt; people with hypertension should check sodium content.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Manufacturing facilities may also process gluten‑containing foods, which is relevant for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve yellow rice hot as a side dish with meat, fish, vegetable stews, or legume dishes. It can be used in salads, casseroles, or as a base for pilaf. Add fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or toasted nuts for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked yellow rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in bags at –18 °C or lower. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving.
